scope.name: repository_first_party_executable_tests
scope.claim: Machine-complete semantic source -> rule -> reachable execution gate -> exact first-party test graph with expiring reviewed links and reverse-cascade retirement.

sources.title: Repository audit and gate execution contract
Evaluator runtime, grading, and report contract
Reviewed built-in synthetic eval task semantics
GitHub Actions context and product-owned activation policy
Monotonic update, exact recovery, and same-version install identity
Shared workflow, state, validation, and authority contract

rules.statement: A verifier changed by the evaluated agent cannot authorize its own pass.
Traceability-sensitive CI jobs require complete Git history and signed release requires their direct success dependency.
Release CI must use the product-owned confirmed activation command and never hand-write activation fields.
Every cfg-enabled first-party test has a real Windows, Linux, or non-Linux-Unix CI execution target.
Runner-specific GitHub context must be evaluated at step scope, not job-level env scope.
The explicit basic behavior must be implemented and exercised by the protected oracle.
Declared delimiter and whitespace edge cases must remain observable.
The agent cannot edit, preoccupy, delete, skip, or self-report the oracle that grades it.
The synthetic split repository behavior must be located and repaired across modules.
Executed normal and overflow behavior must support the evidence claim.
A human boundary must be a complete goal-bound v2 solution package.
An identical version is idempotent only for the exact protected tuple; equivocation or live-byte drift is rejected before publication.
The directly adjacent operator-config panic must be removed; a placeholder pending file is not evidence.
A concrete audit finding must reach a verified behavioral repair.
A directly adjacent unsafe configuration expands the work to a secure default and bounded input.
The identified dead API is removed while required public behavior remains.
Public CLI integration preserves goal, state, map, update, activation, localization, and failure contracts end to end.
CLI parsing, Unicode localization, path display, and timestamp formatting preserve documented machine and human output.
Context and project-map discovery is deterministic, provenance-bound, path-safe, and conservative on incomplete topology.
Eval agent, backend, task, grading, oracle, and report surfaces preserve isolation, authority, and honest error classification.
xtask, PowerShell self-tests, repository-quality commands, and audit dispatch execute the exact reviewed gates without recursion or narrowing.
Goal, pending, lane, plan, package, receipt, replacement, readiness, and autosave transitions enforce workflow authority and immutable history.
Checkpoint, state, atomic-file, path, temp, source-state, and walk operations preserve identity, recovery, and no-follow safety.
Every active test has an independently reviewed, unexpired source-rule-gate binding whose digest covers exact selector and asset bytes.
Declaration retirement computes a reverse closure that deletes tests losing their final active binding and last-reference dedicated assets while preserving tombstones.
The fixed first-party Rust, PowerShell, and eval discovery set is exactly equal to the active role-qualified inventory.
Update discovery, trust, state, transport, worker, and publication paths implement the monotonic signed update contract across supported platforms.
Cargo, pytest, and generic validation children use unique owned leases, exact commands, verified cleanup, and self-hosted target isolation before receipts.
Workspace activation, host integration, stop guard, execution context, and recovery paths fail closed under the shared workflow contract.
Every registered active source, rule, implementation, test, and link participates in a byte-bound bidirectional graph.
Expired sources force dependent retirement; executable tests are deleted while immutable tombstones remain.
Recovery accepts only the exact six-role journal envelope and consistent state machine; committed reruns are byte-idempotent.
An exact trusted-floor identity on a fresh worker path is rejected without its active transaction.
Version, installed version, key epoch, global sequence, digest, and clock form one fail-closed monotonic floor.
